statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail holds at 13% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. No pathological one-way price path can form while no venue is quoting.

This hour makes a correction that matters more than any single headline. The preceding hours repeatedly asserted that the Russia-Ukraine energy transmission channel was shut - that no refinery, pipeline or export terminal had been struck, and that the oil route to a Nasdaq problem was therefore closed. That is wrong, and it was wrong when it was written. Ukraine struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex in Bashkortostan and the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl overnight on 5-6 August, the Yaroslavl governor calling it the region's most massive attack of the war. Omsk, Russia's largest refinery, and Saratov both halted after strikes on 6-7 July. The Tuapse terminal has been shut indefinitely since the April-May strike series. The IEA put more than 20% of Russian refining capacity offline in early July, with Ukraine's General Staff claiming 42.7%. The channel is not closed. It has been open for months.

The right conclusion from that correction is not that Stress must jump. It is that the high Stress reading was already correct for a reason the assessment had misidentified. The energy war is a slow burn that the oil market has been pricing continuously - WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52 are the price of it, up roughly 33% and 34% on the year - rather than a discontinuity waiting to happen. Equities have absorbed it: the Nasdaq-100 sits about 2.3% below its 52-week high with VIX on a 14 handle.

Against that, one genuinely new and constructive datum arrived at 09:40 UTC, after last hour's snapshot: Iran's Revolutionary Guards told Washington through a backchannel that they support Tehran's negotiators in the ceasefire talks, per Axios via the Times of Israel liveblog. That speaks directly to the single largest unpriced risk in this book, the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has kept largely blocked since 28 February. It is the first de-escalatory signal in several days.

Stress therefore moves down one point, 79% to 78%, and stays in the high band. One point of mechanical time-to-reopen compression is bought and then more than offset by two points of real de-escalation. Confidence rises to 74% (solid): the evidence set is materially more complete than an hour ago because a standing factual error was found and corrected against primary reporting, but the entire price-path input remains a two-day-old carry-forward, and two sources were unreachable from this environment.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 13% maps to EA_ON for both instruments. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item this hour is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC CME Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window is anchored to it at 22:00-02:00 UTC (00:00-04:00 Berlin) rather than to the generation time. Forecast Tail drifts 13% to 19% through the remaining halt, steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting - turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) at 21:00 UTC and orange (BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES) at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC - then eases back through the watch band and returns to green at 05:00 UTC Monday. That orange is conditional forecast risk, not observed structure.

No US macro release lands inside the next 24 hours. Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first genuinely high-impact print. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and nothing here is a trade instruction.
headline: Correction hour inside the CME weekend halt: the Russia-Ukraine energy channel was never shut - two refineries struck 5-6 August, 20%+ of Russian refining offline - but the oil market has been pricing it all along, so Tail holds at 13% and green while a new IRGC backchannel signal on Hormuz takes Stress down to 78%, Confidence 74%
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first eleven forecast slots sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to session extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit in the solid band rather than the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified from primary sources this hour and unchanged. NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, day range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, the quote page explicitly marking the contract closed as of 14 August; the 52-week range is 22,961.50-30,975.50, putting NQ roughly 2.7% below its 52-week high. VIX 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, 52-week range 13.38-35.30, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40, +1.42% on the day, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent $88.52, +1.67%, +4.20% and +34.43%. US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% carried from the Federal Reserve's H.15 release at the 13 August observation. Nasdaq-100 cash closed Friday at 30,046.14, about 2.3% below its own 52-week high.

The substantive work this hour was a correction, and it is worth stating plainly because it ran through more than twenty consecutive published hours. Those hours asserted that no refinery, pipeline or export terminal had been struck in the Russia-Ukraine war and concluded that the energy transmission channel to the Nasdaq was closed. The record says otherwise. Zelenskyy announced strikes on the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex in Bashkortostan and the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl overnight on 5-6 August, roughly 700 to 1,300 kilometres from the front, with Russia claiming 605 drones intercepted that night and the Yaroslavl governor calling it the most massive attack the region has seen in the war. Omsk - Russia's largest refinery - and Saratov both halted after strikes on 6-7 July. The Tuapse refinery and export terminal has been shut indefinitely since a strike series running 16 April to 27 May, with tanker traffic diverted to Novorossiysk. Russia suspended civilian shipping through the Don-Azov canal and the Kerch Strait after concentrated attacks on tankers in the Sea of Azov. The IEA assessed more than 20% of Russian refining capacity offline in early July; Ukraine's General Staff claimed 42.7%. The channel has been open for months.

What follows from that is not a Stress spike. It is a reattribution. The high Stress reading carried into this hour was directionally right for a reason the assessment had misidentified, and the correct framing is that the energy war is a continuous slow burn the oil complex has been repricing all year - WTI up about 33% and Brent about 34% year-on-year, the IEA forecasting the widest global supply deficit in five years, and the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve below 300 million barrels for the first time since January 1983 - rather than a latent discontinuity that has not yet fired. A channel that has been transmitting for six months is largely in the price. Equities are the evidence for that: the Nasdaq-100 is 2.3% below its 52-week high and implied volatility closed on a 14 handle. Scoring this as newly-discovered upside risk would be double-counting something the tape has already absorbed.

The Middle East configuration is where the genuinely unpriced risk still sits, and this hour it improved. Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz largely blocked since 28 February; the reinstated US naval blockade has redirected dozens of vessels; Trump cancelled a planned strike on 1 August to allow negotiations; Iran published a restrictive draft plan for the strait on 6 August that pushed oil higher; and crude rose about 5% on Monday 10 August as a deal looked less likely, with Trump telling Axios the US is 'only semi-negotiating'. Against that hardening, the Times of Israel liveblog added an entry at 12:40 IDT - 09:40 UTC, after last hour's snapshot - reporting via Axios that the IRGC has told Washington through a backchannel that it supports Tehran's negotiators in the ceasefire talks. The Revolutionary Guards backing the negotiating track rather than undercutting it is a meaningful constructive datum on the one channel that could still reprice the index violently. It is the first de-escalatory signal in several days and it is scored as such.

The Lebanon track is unchanged on re-check and is not re-counted. The newest market-relevant entries remain the 08:29 IDT IDF confirmation naming Ali Muhammad Fakhr al-Din as the second senior Hezbollah commander killed at Deir al-Zahrani after a Hezbollah drone attack seriously wounded three soldiers, with Lebanese media reporting 11 deaths from the Israeli response. The IDF has not acknowledged claims of overnight fire in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah's answer to Saturday's decapitation strikes has still not been delivered, and that undelivered retaliation remains the sharpest near-term tail in the book.

The cross-asset set remains internally conflicting, and conflict is a Stress input rather than a Tail input. Index futures and cash are near - not at - 52-week highs, implied volatility is priced for calm on a 14 handle, duration is bid rather than offered, and only crude is expressing a geopolitical premium. Nothing in it is aligned into a one-way equity structure, and none of it can be aligned into one while the venue is shut. dominantMode stays mixed.

Why Stress goes down rather than up. The rule adopted at 05:00 UTC still governs: a Stress point has to be bought by new evidence, and it cuts both ways. One point is bought upward by time-to-reopen compression, which is genuine because the quantity of unpriced weekend risk waiting for a single thin auction increases mechanically as that auction approaches. Two points are bought downward by the IRGC backchannel report, which is new, dated after the last snapshot, sourced to Axios, and directed at the largest unpriced risk in the book. Net minus one, 79% to 78%, still high band. The energy-channel correction contributes zero net points, because it changes the explanation rather than the quantity.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour and unchanged. The next seven days contain no CPI, PPI, PCE, NFP or FOMC rate decision. Empire State and NAHB on Monday, then a dense Tuesday - Housing Starts and Building Permits at 12:30 UTC with Export and Import Prices and the NY Fed Services survey alongside, Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 13:15 UTC, Pending Home Sales at 14:00 UTC - the July FOMC minutes Wednesday at 18:00 UTC alongside a 20-year auction at 17:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey Thursday at 12:30 UTC, and the S&P Global flash PMIs Friday at 13:45 UTC. Retail earnings dominate the corporate week - Home Depot Tuesday, Target, Lowe's and TJX Wednesday, Walmart Thursday - so no megacap or semiconductor print capable of creating index-level one-way structure falls inside the window. The two largest scheduled catalysts sit just outside the seven days and are correctly absent from the events array: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 report on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August.

Why Tail stays at 13%: the strategy-killing condition is persistent directional efficiency with failed retracements and repeated extension. With no venue quoting there is no efficiency, no retracement and no extension to observe, and the last observed session was a quiet -0.15% futures drift inside a 254-point range, corroborated by a -0.13% cash close. Nothing in a closed market can promote a headline into a price path, however large the headline - and that holds for a corrected headline just as much as a new one.

Research note on egress: Reuters was unreachable from this environment and both CNBC and HNGN returned HTTP 403. The Hormuz and refinery material was therefore verified against Euronews, Al Jazeera, Wikipedia's Russian fuel crisis and Tuapse articles, and Trading Economics commodity reporting instead of the blocked originals. Investing.com, Trading Economics and the Times of Israel liveblog all fetched cleanly.

lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 10:00 UTC Saturday to 09:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours, and the action was EA_ON, the status green and dominantMode mixed for all 24. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 13%. Stress carried the movement: 52, 53, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then 70, 71, 71, 78 and 79.

Three features of that track matter for reading the current hour. The first nineteen slots are a near-monotonic climb across a market that never quoted once, in which each hour re-priced the same standing Middle East headlines slightly higher rather than re-testing them. The 05:00 slot is the deliberate correction that stopped it, taken after re-verifying Friday's cross-asset marks against primary sources, and the flat 70-71-71 stretch reflects the rule adopted there, that a Stress point must be bought by new evidence. The 08:00 slot's seven-point step to 78% added the Russia-Ukraine theatre, which the preceding 23 slots had omitted entirely.

The third feature is only visible now. Across that entire span the assessment held that the Russia-Ukraine energy transmission channel was closed because no refinery or export terminal had been struck. That premise was false throughout, and the current hour corrects it rather than inheriting it. Past opinions are not rewritten - each slot records what was published at the time, and Confidence rebuilding from 60% to 73% over the window records genuine verification work on the price marks - but the correction is why this hour does not simply extend the Stress ramp.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 09:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first eleven hours after it are inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for 11 of 24 slots, drifting 13% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 24%, 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 05:00 UTC Monday. The forecast status is yellow (WATCH) at 21:00 UTC, orange (BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES) at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 04:00 UTC Monday.

Stress rises from 78% to a 79% plateau across 13:00-22:00 UTC into the reopen and deliberately stops short of the extreme band, then eases to 71% by 09:00 UTC Monday as live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. The plateau rather than a spike is the point. Unpriced weekend risk does compound while the venue is shut, but the largest standing risk in the book - the energy channel - has been transmitting continuously for months and is substantially in the oil price already, and the IRGC's backchannel support for Tehran's negotiators cuts against an escalatory reopen. Extreme Stress should be reserved for a channel that is opening, not one that has been open and absorbed.

Confidence decays from 74% to 65% as Friday's marks age through the remaining halt, then recovers to 78% after the restart, a larger recovery than the decay because a live price path is the single missing input and the rest of the evidence set is now materially more complete. The seven slots spanning 21:00 UTC to 03:00 UTC switch to event/whipsaw for a thin opening auction that has to absorb a full weekend at once, including an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation.

No US macro release falls inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first high-impact catalyst. The forecast Tail path is conditional risk, not an assertion that any future price structure has already been observed.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour, still inside the CME weekend halt. No venue quoting, so no price path can form and Tail stays low at 13%. Stress eases one point as the IRGC backchannel datum offsets an hour of reopen compression.
Thin European Sunday. No scheduled catalyst and no live tape; the only thing that changes is the age of Friday's marks. Confidence begins its slow decay from 74%.
Midday UTC. Tail drifts to 14% purely as time-to-reopen risk, not as observed structure. Stress holds at 78% absent new headlines from either theatre.
Stress steps to 79% as the window of unpriced weekend risk narrows toward a single restart auction. Still high band, still short of extreme.
Tail 15%. Any Middle East or Ukraine headline arriving now has no venue on which to be priced, which defers rather than removes the risk.
Late European afternoon. Evidence set is unchanged and ageing; Confidence 71%. Nothing here promotes a headline into a price path.
